passage:
"I don't read the news any more," Kavitha said, pushing her plate away. "Every channel lied about the flood numbers. Every single one."
"So you believe nothing now?" Ayesha asked.
"Correct. Nothing."
"Then a forward saying the tap water is poisoned is as true as the newspaper?"
"No, but..." Kavitha stopped. "Fine. That's different."
"Not by much. If you trust nothing, whoever shouts loudest steers you, same as if you trusted everything."
Kavitha tore a piece of roti. "Okay. Which ones would you keep?"
"The ones that print corrections when they get it wrong. The local daily does. That bulletin on the radio does too."
"Two sources," Kavitha said. "And I decide slowly."
"Slowly is fine. Nobody needs certainty by dinner 🙂"

qa.q: Which two sources did Ayesha say print corrections?
qa.a: Ayesha named the local daily and the bulletin on the radio.

qa.q: Why did Kavitha say no news could be trusted any more?
qa.a: Kavitha felt that every channel lied about the flood numbers, so trust in all of them collapsed.

qa.q: How can Kavitha handle a new headline under the new plan?
qa.a: Look at the two sources that print corrections, decide slowly and hold the conclusion loosely until more is known.

qa.q: How does Ayesha see trusting no news at all?
qa.a: Ayesha sees it as another way to be steered, because whoever shouts loudest would win, just as with blind trust.

grounding: After repeated lies, total distrust of news is as manipulable as blind trust; a few sources with track records of corrections and loosely held conclusions.
